context.note:
ELIXIR-DEV implemented REQ-194 (Prometheus metrics subsystem, OBS-02) strictly per the CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR-approved design (lib/letflow/design/req194-prometheus-metrics.md), which PASSED with no gaps found. This is a tenant-data-path-ADJACENT change requiring this hard gate for two distinct reasons: (a) it adds a NEW GLOBAL, UNAUTHENTICATED HTTP route (GET /metrics) outside every existing auth boundary, whose entire safety rests on a label-allowlist invariant rather than authentication/tenant-scoping -- exactly the class of decision INV-1/INV-6 exist to have you verify independently; (b) it adds a new direct mix.exs dependency needing explicit sign-off.

FLAG 1 -- NEW DIRECT DEPENDENCY (please record explicit sign-off for this specific line): mix.exs now has `{:telemetry, "~> 1.4"}`. This is a PROMOTION, not a new fetch: mix.lock already resolved :telemetry v1.4.2 transitively via bandit/db_connection/ecto/ecto_sql/plug (confirmed identical -- `git diff mix.lock` is EMPTY, `git diff --stat mix.exs mix.lock` shows only mix.exs changed, 12 lines added, zero lines removed). Zero new bytes fetched, zero new transitive tree, zero new license surface (Apache-2.0, already accepted transitively). CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's own step-02a handoff already characterizes this precisely (see context.dependency_promotion_flag_for_reviewer there) and recommends REVIEWER weigh it as a promotion-to-direct, not a new-dependency-adoption review -- but REQ-194's own AC3 draws no size-based exception, so sign-off is still required in this PR before Step 2d's REVIEWER gate, per the design's own §10.

FLAG 2 -- THE LABEL-ALLOWLIST INVARIANT IS THE ENTIRE SAFETY MECHANISM FOR AN UNAUTHENTICATED, GLOBAL ENDPOINT (please verify every emission call site yourself, not just trust this note): `GET /metrics` (lib/letflow/routers/metrics_exposition.ex) is mounted on Letflow.Router OUTSIDE Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline/AuthPipeline entirely -- no session/token check of any kind, one process-wide Letflow.Metrics.Registry (lib/letflow/metrics/registry.ex), no per-tenant branching. This is safe ONLY because every one of the six metric families' label set is a fixed, hand-built allow-list that NEVER extracts a tenant_id/definition_id/instance_id/task_id/actor_id from event metadata into a label -- not filtered at exposition time, but never extracted in the first place, at each handle_* function in registry.ex. Please read every handle_task_completed/3, handle_event_append_stop/3, handle_repo_query/3, handle_http_request/3 function body in lib/letflow/metrics/registry.ex yourself and confirm none of them can ever emit an identifying value. In particular: family 2 (task_completions_total) is labelled `definition_status` (a closed 4-value enum: draft|active|deprecated|archived) -- NEVER definition_id or a definition name, which is a deliberate RESTATEMENT of R-Co's literal 'labelled by definition' wording (design §1's own reasoning, cited in metrics_exposition.ex's moduledoc). HTTP-request/error labels (families 5/6) use route TEMPLATE via Plug.Router.match_path/1 (never the raw request path), so a UUID in a URL path parameter can never reach a label either.

WHAT CHANGED (full list):
(1) mix.exs -- added {:telemetry, "~> 1.4"} (see FLAG 1).
(2) lib/letflow/metrics/registry.ex (NEW) -- GenServer owning a named public ETS table (:letflow_metrics), attaches via :telemetry.attach_many/4 to [:letflow, :task, :completed], [:letflow, :event_store, :append, :stop], [:letflow, :repo, :query], [:letflow, :http, :request]. Family 1 (active_instances) is deliberately NOT :telemetry-driven -- called directly by Letflow.Scheduler.Poller via set_active_instances/1 and mark_active_instances_refresh_failed/0 (design §5/§6's own stated exception; the moduledoc explains why).
(3) lib/letflow/metrics/exposition.ex (NEW) -- pure function, Registry.snapshot/0 in, Prometheus exposition text out. Never calls Letflow.Repo (this is what makes the DB-unavailable graceful-degradation contract structural, not best-effort, for families 2-6).
(4) lib/letflow/plugs/http_metrics.ex (NEW) -- Plug mounted on Letflow.Router ahead of :match/:dispatch, emits [:letflow, :http, :request] via register_before_send/2. Excludes GET /metrics itself (no self-observation feedback loop). CORRECTION TO THE DESIGN'S OWN TEXT, flagged for your attention: design §2 claims conn.private[:plug_route] is UNSET on an unmatched request; verified against real Plug source (deps/plug/lib/plug/router.ex:663) that this is not quite right -- Plug.Router's own `match _` catch-all rewrites to the literal path \"/*_path\", which IS recorded, so match_path/1 does not raise there. The cardinality-safety property the design wants still holds -- this module detects the \"/*_path\" wildcard suffix explicitly (at any forward-nesting depth) and maps it to the same literal \"unmatched\" constant the design specifies. Documented in the module's own moduledoc under 'Correction to design §2's stated mechanism'.
(5) lib/letflow/routers/metrics_exposition.ex (NEW) -- GET /metrics, Plug.Router, Content-Type \"text/plain; version=0.0.4\", no auth, no Repo call. Moduledoc restates all three REQ-078 divergence decisions (auth/scope/format) with reasons, verbatim per this requirement's own convention, per AC1.
(6) lib/letflow/router.ex -- mounts Letflow.Plugs.HttpMetrics (ahead of :match/:dispatch, alongside Cors) and forward(\"/metrics\", to: Letflow.Routers.MetricsExposition), declared before the /api/v1 forward (same tier as /health, /api/tenant-config -- no tenant context to resolve, no session to check).
(7) lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex -- removed forward(\"/metrics\", to: Letflow.Routers.Metrics) (the retired per-tenant JSON endpoint's mount).
(8) lib/letflow/routers/metrics.ex -- DELETED entirely (REQ-078's placeholder, whose own moduledoc anticipated exactly this supersession). Letflow.Api.Authorization's :MetricsRead permission atom and endpoint_policy_key(\"GET\", \"/metrics\") clause are left in place, unused, per design §9/§10's own explicit open-question disposition -- NOT pruned in this diff (a separate, later cleanup requirement's job).
(9) lib/letflow/application.ex -- added Letflow.Metrics.Registry to the supervision tree, directly after {Registry, keys: :unique, name: Letflow.Registry} (a leaf, independently-startable component with no startup-order dependents).
(10) lib/letflow/engine.ex -- new private emit_task_completed_telemetry/2, called between Repo.transaction/2 and interpret_complete_result/1 inside run_complete_task/6 (i.e. strictly AFTER the transaction has committed). Resolves definition_status via a separate Letflow.Definitions.get_by_id/2 call (not re-derivable from anything already in scope at that point -- design §12 open question 3 left this to ELIXIR-DEV's judgment). Best-effort: any lookup failure silently skips telemetry emission rather than raising (INV-8 -- a metrics side-effect must never turn a real, successful task completion into an error).
(11) lib/letflow/event_store.ex -- wraps the existing Repo.transaction/2 call inside append/2 with :telemetry.span/3 (event prefix [:letflow, :event_store, :append]). Preserves append/2's existing {:ok, _}/{:error, _} return contract exactly (span/3 re-raises/returns the wrapped function's own result unchanged).
(12) lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex -- handle_info(:tick, state) restructured: tenant_schemas/0 (pre-existing) is now wrapped by a new fetch_tenant_schemas/0 (catches a raised DBConnection error, e.g. the DB fully unreachable) and a new maybe_refresh_active_instances/1 + count_active_for_schema/1 (catches a single tenant schema's own query failure in isolation, contributing 0 to the platform-wide sum rather than crashing or zeroing the whole aggregate). FLAGGED DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM THE DESIGN'S OWN LITERAL WORDING (also flagged in the module's own moduledoc): design §6 says 'the timer poll-and-fire loop for that tick still proceeds normally' even when tenant_schemas/0 itself raises -- but that loop's own input IS tenant_schemas/0's result, so this implementation skips BOTH the poll-and-fire loop and the active-instances refresh for that one tick when tenant_schemas/0 itself fails (calling mark_active_instances_refresh_failed/0), rather than attempting either against an empty/undefined list. Please confirm this is an acceptable, non-scope-creeping reading of design §6's intent (crash-avoidance is preserved; only the precise 'proceeds normally' wording is not literal).
(13) Test files: test/letflow/api/authorization_enforcement_test.exs and test/letflow/routers/req078_supporting_routes_test.exs updated to remove references to the deleted Letflow.Routers.Metrics (AC9's own route-table introspection and per-tenant-scoping tests, both now retired since the module they tested is gone). New test files listed above cover AC2/AC4/AC5/AC6/AC7/AC8/AC9 (see step-02a's own task acceptance_criteria) as a good-faith initial pass -- TEST-DESIGNER performs the definitive coverage gap-check at Step 3.

VERIFICATION ALREADY DONE BY ELIXIR-DEV (please re-run independently, do not just trust this report): mix deps.get (telemetry stays at 1.4.2, no new packages), mix compile --warnings-as-errors (clean, 0 warnings), mix format --check-formatted (clean), mix letflow.lint_handoffs (0 new violations, 25 pre-existing grandfathered per ISS-0190), git diff --stat mix.exs mix.lock (mix.exs +12/-0 lines, mix.lock EMPTY diff). Ran the 4 new test files (20/20 passing), all directly-touched existing test files (req078_supporting_routes_test.exs, authorization_enforcement_test.exs, router_test.exs, poller_test.exs, engine_complete_task_test.exs, scheduler_test.exs, event_store_test.exs -- 108/109, the one unrelated failure was a pre-existing environmental issue in a shared long-lived test database traced to a stale tenant_schemas registration from an unrelated prior run, not a regression from this diff, and was resolved by rewriting the affected new test to avoid depending on that shared table's hygiene rather than touching the failing legacy schema), and a broader sweep (application_test.exs, engine_cancel_instance_test.exs, engine_variable_schema_merge_test.exs, engine_execution_error_test.exs, engine_sub_process_test.exs, engine_concurrency_test.exs, test/letflow/event_store/, test/letflow/api/ -- 366/366 passing). Could not run the full `mix test` suite synchronously within this environment's tool timeout (whole-suite runs exceed 10 minutes on this host) -- targeted, directly-relevant coverage above is what was actually run and quoted.

task.description: SECURITY-REVIEWER hard gate (WF-02 Step 2c) on REQ-194's implementation. Read the approved design (lib/letflow/design/req194-prometheus-metrics.md) and the real shipped code in full before verdict, per docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md. This diff's risk profile is unusual for this project: it adds Letflow's FIRST global, unauthenticated, cross-tenant-visible HTTP endpoint by deliberate design (see design §1 Axis 2/3's reasoning) -- your job is to independently verify the label-allowlist invariant that makes this safe actually holds, by reading every :telemetry handler in lib/letflow/metrics/registry.ex yourself, not by trusting this handoff's note. Also record explicit sign-off on the new direct :telemetry dependency in mix.exs (FLAG 1 in context.note) -- required by REQ-194's own AC3 regardless of the promotion's lighter risk profile. PASS/FAIL routes to REVIEWER next per WF-02 Step 2d.
acceptance_criteria: INV-1/INV-6: confirm no metric family's label allow-list, anywhere in lib/letflow/metrics/registry.ex, can ever extract a tenant_id/definition_id/instance_id/task_id/actor_id value from event metadata into a label -- read every handle_* function body directly, not just this note's description of them

confirm the mix.exs {:telemetry, "~> 1.4"} line is recorded with explicit REVIEWER/SECURITY-REVIEWER sign-off in this requirement's PR, weighing it correctly as a promotion of an already-transitively-present dependency (git diff mix.lock is empty) rather than a new-dependency-adoption risk review, per REQ-194's own AC3

confirm GET /metrics is genuinely unreachable through any authenticated/tenant-scoped path that could smuggle a different label set in (it is mounted before the /api/v1 forward, structurally outside Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline/AuthPipeline)

confirm lib/letflow/engine.ex's new emit_task_completed_telemetry/2 cannot turn a successful task completion into an error (INV-8) -- its Definitions.get_by_id/2 lookup failure path must silently skip telemetry, never raise or propagate an error tuple that changes complete_task/3's existing return contract

confirm lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex's new DB-unreachable handling (fetch_tenant_schemas/0, count_active_for_schema/1) cannot itself crash the Poller GenServer on any realistic Postgres failure mode, and record a view on the flagged deviation from design §6's literal 'proceeds normally' wording (context.note point 12)

confirm the removal of lib/letflow/routers/metrics.ex and the retained-but-unused :MetricsRead permission atom does not reopen any authorization gap (no route now resolves to that atom, so its retained-but-orphaned state is inert)

result.summary: REQ-194's Prometheus metrics subsystem passes the SECURITY-REVIEWER gate. INV-1/INV-4/INV-6/INV-7/INV-8 apply and are satisfied; INV-2/INV-3/INV-5 remain NOT-APPLICABLE (S4/S5 not started). The label-allowlist invariant that makes GET /metrics safe as a global, unauthenticated endpoint was independently verified by reading every handle_*/dispatch clause in lib/letflow/metrics/registry.ex line by line: no metric family can ever extract a tenant_id/instance_id/definition_id/task_id/actor_id into a label. family 2 is confirmed labelled definition_status (closed 4-value enum) only. lib/letflow/plugs/http_metrics.ex's route-template labeling was confirmed to only ever emit Plug.Router.match_path/1's compile-time template or the literal 'unmatched' constant, never a raw path. ELIXIR-DEV's correction re: conn.private[:plug_route] being always-set (including on Plug.Router's own match _ catch-all, rewritten to "/*_path" via extract_path/1) was verified against the real deps/plug/lib/plug/router.ex source directly and is accurate; the 'unmatched' fallback never concatenates with any composed path fragment. The flagged Poller DB-unavailable deviation from design section 6's literal 'proceeds normally' wording was assessed and judged a safe, correctly-reasoned adaptation (the literal wording is internally incoherent on the raise path), not a defect requiring CODE-DESIGNER rework. The new direct {:telemetry, "~> 1.4"} mix.exs dependency is signed off by SECURITY-REVIEWER as a zero-new-risk promotion of an already-resolved transitive dependency (mix.lock diff empty) -- REVIEWER still owes its own AC3 sign-off on this line before merge. Full findings: handoffs/WF02-REQ194-20260830/security-review-req194.md.
